scope: Experimental candidate-stage control only. CPU directory encoded by the runtime-source Rust encoder feeds a GPU procedural TLAS, raw leaf buffers and an incomplete shader 219 candidate helper. This does not execute whole 219 or attach anything to the provider.
directory: Version 1: 16-byte header; per-TLAS-instance 16-byte candidate ranges including disabled entries; 16-byte candidate entries map primitive index to an aligned 64-byte leaf and side. Root constants provide physical byte extents because root SRVs have no size.
assertions: Valid synthetic candidates have the same commit status, instance, primitive, and numeric distance as the existing TRI0 fixture; positive and negative zero compare numerically equal and raw bits are recorded.
Conservatively unsupported miss numerics set status bit 4. This makes the whole result invalid for consumption; the harness uses a private output only to inspect candidate behavior.
An intentionally truncated 15-byte physical directory extent sets status bit 2 and commits no candidates.
limitations: The candidate helper deliberately rejects ordinary misses as unsupported and does not implement full 219 control flow, native reciprocal precision, general hardware arithmetic or ray culling.
The Rust encoder and GPU helper are not linked to live provider dispatch or queue-ordered AS provenance.
GPU status is read only by the control after completion; in real command lists later commands could consume output before the CPU observes failure. This is not fail-closed for live dispatch.
Geometric bounds, transforms, sidecar ownership, descriptor association, aliasing, compaction, replay and cross-queue lifetimes are not established.
